name: Question 11
problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{3{x}^{2}+4}{5},\,0<x<1
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{20},$ compute $\text{E}[2X-{X}^{3}+1].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X-{X}^{3}+1] & =2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[{X}^{3}]+\text{E}[1] \\  & =2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[{X}^{3}]+1\end{aligned}
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the third raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\cdot (\frac{3{x}^{2}+4}{5})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{3}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{4}{5}{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{1}{10}{x}^{6}+\frac{1}{5}{x}^{4})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=\frac{11}{20}$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{3}]=\frac{3}{10}$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X-{X}^{3}+1] & =2\text{E}[X]-\text{E}[{X}^{3}]+1 \\  & =2\cdot \frac{11}{20}-\frac{3}{10}+1 \\  & =\frac{11}{10}-\frac{3}{10}+1 \\  & =\frac{9}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

The continuous random variable X has the following probability density function:

f(x)=3x2+45,0<x<1

Given that E[X]=1120, compute E[2X−X3+1].

Hint: You may assume that E[aX+bY]=aE[X]+bE[Y] for any random variables X and Y and constants a and b.

a
710
b
1710
c
95
d
1910
e
45
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

E[2X−X3+1]=2E[X]−E[X3]+E[1]=2E[X]−E[X3]+1

For a continuous random variable X with probability density function f(x) defined over a set S, the nth raw moment of X is given by

E[Xn]=∫Sxn⋅f(x)dx.

We already know E[X]. So, we compute the third raw moment of X as follows: E[X3]=∫01x3⋅(3x2+45)dx=∫01(35x5+45x3)dx=(110x6+15x4)|01=110+15=310

Substituting E[X]=1120 and E[X3]=310 into the simplified expression, we conclude that

E[2X−X3+1]=2E[X]−E[X3]+1=2⋅1120−310+1=1110−310+1=95.
